final_answer.key_evidence_summary: Object/address layers are clean: all 11 pods 2/2 Running with 0 restarts, all 11 Deployments 1/1 AVAILABLE, every Service has endpoints bound, and active TCP probes to all 11 service:port pairs returned 'Connection Succeeded' — excluding scheduling, image-pull, probe, selector, port-mapping and DNS faults. The break is on the code surface: cartservice error logs are flooded (761/2844 lines, ratio 0.268) with a single pattern showing every add-to-cart arriving with arguments inverted — 'AddItemAsync called with userId=9SIQT8TOJO, productId=4fe51a56-1a94-43ce-be91-5958ce17d236, quantity=5', i.e. the product ID in userId and the session UUID in productId (matching frontend's own log line for the same request: product=9SIQT8TOJO, quantity=5, session=4fe51a56-...), while the same pod's GetCartAsync correctly receives the session UUID as userId. Tracing upstream: cartservice's CartService.cs and RedisCartStore.cs pass the fields through correctly, and frontend/rpc.go insertCart uses correct named fields (UserId: userID, Item.ProductId: productID) — but frontend/handlers.go addToCartHandler contains the injected swap 'userID, productID = productID, userID' immediately before fe.insertCart(...). So the caller frontend emits the malformed request (wrong argument order), and cart writes land under a key owned by the product ID, so the session's cart is never updated. The events surface shows only setup history (FailedCreate 'serviceaccount ... not found' each followed by SuccessfulCreate, plus rolling-restart probe noise), so no live infrastructure mechanism exists.
